Lineage-mixed neurodevelopmental programs in pediatric sarcomas nominate tumor-selective surface antigen pairs.

The authors analyzed a pan-pediatric single-cell RNA-seq atlas of 266 samples across 22 pediatric solid tumor types to identify shared developmental gene expression programs. They found that pediatric sarcomas exhibit lineage-mixed neurodevelopmental programs, which they used to nominate tumor-selective surface antigen pairs as potential therapeutic targets. This work demonstrates how single-cell atlases can reveal convergent vulnerabilities in low-mutation-burden pediatric cancers.

HOMED enables hierarchical and multimodal optimization of DNA methylation deconvolution across tissues.

HOMED is a new computational framework for DNA methylation deconvolution that improves estimation of cell-type proportions in bulk tissue samples. It incorporates hierarchical relationships among related cell types, uses single-cell RNA-seq to guide deconvolution, and optimizes CpG signatures with paired bulk RNA-seq/DNAm data. The method aims to generalize better across datasets than existing reference-based approaches.

Cell systems 2026-Oct-29 Medium

Categorization and analysis of 16 computational methods for estimating cell potency from single-cell RNA-seq data.

This review systematically categorizes 16 computational methods for estimating cell potency (differentiation potential) from scRNA-seq data into average-based, entropy-based, and knowledge-based approaches. The authors highlight that these methods rest on different, sometimes contrasting, assumptions, and provide a unified mathematical framework for comparing them. This work helps researchers choose appropriate potency-inference tools and understand their underlying biases.

CellMarker 3.0: an updated resource of manually curated and computationally predicted cell markers in human/mouse and interactive web tools for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics analysis.

CellMarker 3.0 is an updated database of cell-type marker genes for human and mouse, now combining manually curated experimentally validated markers with computationally predicted ones. It adds substantial new content (274 tissues, 1,877 cell types, 64,040 markers, over 1.2 million tissue–cell type–marker entries) and introduces interactive web tools for analyzing single-cell RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics data.

A droplet-based long-read single-cell epigenome sequencing method for the high-throughput profiling of multidimensional regulatory elements within individual cells.

The authors developed droplet-based long-read single-cell epigenome sequencing methods, dscNanoATAC and dscNanoCUT, that combine a commercial microfluidic device with nanopore sequencing to profile chromatin accessibility and histone modifications in individual cells at high throughput. This addresses the previous scalability bottleneck of long-read single-cell epigenomics, enabling multidimensional regulatory element profiling per cell.

Denoising single-cell ATAC-seq data with Shannon entropy.

The authors introduce a Shannon entropy-based method for filtering low-quality droplets in single-cell ATAC-seq data, aiming to remove empty droplets and damaged nuclei that distort downstream analyses. Unlike existing approaches that rely on read depth or predefined genomic features, this method uses the information content of chromatin accessibility profiles to distinguish high-quality nuclei. This could improve the recovery of rare cell populations by reducing noise in scATAC-seq datasets.

SigBridgeR: An R Toolkit for Standardized Identification and Benchmarking of Phenotype-Associated Cell Subpopulations in Single-Cell Transcriptomics.

SigBridgeR is an R toolkit that standardizes the process of identifying and benchmarking cell subpopulations linked to clinical phenotypes by integrating bulk transcriptomic and single-cell RNA-seq data. It addresses the current fragmentation in the field, where diverse computational methods with different algorithms, parameters, and output formats make fair comparison and reproducibility difficult. The toolkit provides a unified framework for method comparison and selection.

Bio Systems 2026-Nov-01 Medium

Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.

The authors propose a per-edge arbitration approach for gene regulatory network inference, training a gradient-boosted classifier on the raw scores from ten different inference methods (including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR, and ARACNe) so that method weighting varies by edge rather than being fixed globally. They also develop a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflicts, evaluated across six single-cell perturbation screens. This reframes method disagreement as a signal to be exploited rather than a nuisance to be averaged away.

Translational oncology 2026-Nov-01 Medium

Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis reveals an epithelial cell-derived prognostic and immunotherapeutic signature with ADAM12 as a key functional regulator in non-small cell lung cancer.

This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data from NSCLC to build a prognostic and immunotherapeutic signature (PIS) based on epithelial cell-derived genes, using machine learning to stratify patients by survival and immune activity. Low-PIS patients showed better outcomes and higher immune infiltration, and ADAM12 was validated as a key functional regulator through tissue/cell-line expression and cellular assays. The work combines signature development with experimental validation of a candidate gene.

Trends in genetics : TIG 2026-Nov-01 Medium

A categorization of spatial transcriptomics methods for cell-cell communication analysis.

This review organizes 33 recent computational methods for inferring cell-cell communication from spatial transcriptomics data into three categories: cell-type or single-cell resolution network inference, modeling of microenvironment-driven transcriptional variability, and regulatory modulation. It highlights how spatial context enables more biologically grounded communication inference than scRNA-seq alone and maps methods to the distinct biological questions they address.

A contextual activity score (CAS) for inferring ADAR-associated transcriptional activity across RNA-seq, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics.

The authors introduce a Contextual Activity Score (CAS) that infers ADAR-associated RNA editing activity from gene expression data rather than raw sequencing reads. This overcomes the limitations of the standard Alu Editing Index, which requires raw reads and performs poorly on single-cell and spatial transcriptomics. CAS enables ADAR activity estimation across RNA-seq, single-cell, and spatial platforms.

An integrated transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulatory circuit orchestrated by NUDT21 maintains the proliferation and survival of neuroblastoma.

This study investigates how alternative polyadenylation (APA), a post-transcriptional regulatory mechanism, contributes to neuroblastoma, the most common pediatric solid tumor. The authors identify NUDT21 as a central regulator that coordinates both transcriptional and post-transcriptional circuits to sustain neuroblastoma cell proliferation and survival, suggesting APA machinery as a potential therapeutic target.

Frontiers in immunology 2026--01 Low

Decoding pyroptosis at single-cell resolution: heterogeneity, microenvironment remodeling and potential translational insights.

This review examines how single-cell RNA sequencing is being used to study pyroptosis, an inflammatory form of programmed cell death driven by caspases and Gasdermin proteins. The authors argue that scRNA-seq overcomes the limitations of bulk RNA-seq by revealing cell-to-cell heterogeneity in pyroptotic gene expression and by mapping how pyroptosis reshapes the surrounding microenvironment through intercellular communication. The paper also discusses potential translational implications of these single-cell insights.

Reanalysis of public bulk and single-nucleus transcriptomes identifies widespread tumor-normal dysregulation and a cross-layer cell-cycle signal in sinonasal squamous cell carcinoma.

This study reanalyzes public bulk and single-nucleus transcriptome data to characterize sinonasal squamous cell carcinoma (SNSCC), a rare head and neck cancer, comparing tumor versus normal tissue and HPV-positive versus HPV-negative cases. The authors report widespread tumor-normal transcriptional dysregulation and identify a cell-cycle signal that appears consistently across both bulk and single-nucleus data layers. The work provides a descriptive transcriptomic resource for an understudied cancer type.
